title: Restriction to a closed support detects the zero action on supported cohomology
statement:
Use the finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, and twists $A(t)$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use ordinary and supported pro-etale cohomology [def-pur-support-cohomology], the supported cup product [def-pur-supported-cup], and its ordinary pullback and twist identifications [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality]. For integers $a,b\geq0$ and $t,s\in\mathbf Z$, let $\alpha\in H^a(X,A(t))$ and $\beta\in H^b_Z(X,A(s))$. If $i^*\alpha=0$ in $H^a(Z,A(t))$, then
$$\alpha\cup\beta=0\quad\text{in }H^{a+b}_Z(X,A(t+s)),\qquad \alpha\cup\operatorname{forg}(\beta)=0\quad\text{in }H^{a+b}(X,A(t+s)).$$
Here $\operatorname{forg}$ is the canonical map forgetting support. No smoothness, regularity, Cartier, or purity hypothesis on $X$ or $Z$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0G75 (remark-support-cup-product), 0G76 (remark-support-cup-product-global), 0G77 (lemma-support-cup-product): closed-support action and forgetting support; the statement is their ordinary finite-coefficient pro-etale analogue, not an application of a ringed-space theorem to a site
